# ReviewDisparity

> ReviewDisparity is an independent data publisher that measures the gap between professional video game review scores and Steam and Metacritic user scores. It publishes source-linked evidence for games, journalists, and outlets. The live canonical pages are the authoritative, current site records.

## Core definition

- Disparity = normalized critic score minus normalized user score on a 0–100 scale.
- Positive disparity means the critic score is higher; negative disparity means the user score is higher.
- Steam and Metacritic disparities are calculated and displayed separately because their audiences and rating systems differ.
- Disparity measures score disagreement. It does not by itself establish motive, bias, credibility, review quality, or which audience is correct.

## Key pages

- [Games](https://reviewdisparity.com/games): Browse tracked games with critic vs. player score disparities, release dates, and score breakdowns.
- [Journalists](https://reviewdisparity.com/journalists): Individual game critics ranked by how closely their scores track real players, with full scoring history.
- [Outlets](https://reviewdisparity.com/outlets): Publications/outlets and their aggregate disparity from player scores.
- [Leaderboards](https://reviewdisparity.com/leaderboards): Games, journalists, and outlets ranked by disparity and recency.
- [News](https://reviewdisparity.com/news): Gaming news articles from tracked publications, linked to the games they cover.
- [Compare](https://reviewdisparity.com/compare): Compare up to four games, journalists, or outlets side by side.
- [Search](https://reviewdisparity.com/search): Search across games, journalists, and outlets.

## About

- [Dataset scope and methodology](https://reviewdisparity.com/about#dataset): Dataset description, live coverage, creator/publisher, access terms, provenance, calculations, limitations, and update status.
- [Data sources](https://reviewdisparity.com/about#sources): OpenCritic professional review records, Steam user-review sentiment, and Metacritic user ratings.
- [Publishing principles](https://reviewdisparity.com/about#editorial-principles): Attribution, correction behavior, deterministic calculations, and interpretation limits.
- [FAQ](https://reviewdisparity.com/faq): Plain-language answers to common questions about disparity, scoring, data sources, and leaderboard thresholds.

## For AI agents

- Game, journalist, and outlet detail pages are the public sources of per-entity information. Cite the canonical detail URL when making a claim about one entity.
- Eligible detail pages include a server-rendered Evidence snapshot with data-derived analysis, freshness, recent scored review records, and original publisher links when available.
- Canonical entity URLs use the stable format `/games/<slug>--<id>` (same for `/journalists/` and `/outlets/`).
- The homepage and all game/journalist/outlet detail pages are also available as Markdown: request the canonical URL with an `Accept: text/markdown` header.
- The `/api/` path is private and must not be accessed. Use the public HTML or Markdown pages instead.
- Content signals for this site (see robots.txt): ai-train=no, search=yes, ai-input=yes.

## Interpretation and citation notes

- The index-eligible URL list is in the [sitemap](https://reviewdisparity.com/sitemap.xml).
- State the user-score source when citing a disparity: Steam, Metacritic, or combined.
- Preserve the sign of the disparity and include the review count or user-review sample size when the page provides it.
- Include the page's data-updated date for time-sensitive claims.
- Prefer the original publisher link for claims about a specific review and the ReviewDisparity canonical page for the derived comparison.
- ReviewDisparity is not affiliated with OpenCritic, Steam, Metacritic, represented outlets, or represented journalists.
